game.name: Paper Planet
game.short_description: Paper Planet is a planet-defender, arcade roguelike with a doodley, Flash-inspired artstyle. Battle through waves of unique enemies and bosses. Combine items with strange and wacky effects for insanely overpowered runs. Play with 1-4 players, for some chaotic co-op fun!

commentary.label: Tier list Part 3 (2025)
commentary.summary: Paper Planet is a cute, hand-drawn, paper-styled bullet-hell roguelike where you defend a small planet with a turret that slides left and right and teleports to the opposite side. Runs are extremely chaotic and usually end with the screen flooded with bullets. He enjoys the vibe, the simple core loop and the boss fights, but finds runs too samey, the meta progression weak, and the game too easily overpowered. He calls it a fun mess worth a few runs and places it in B tier for now.
praise: Cute hand-drawn paper visuals with a Flash-game vibe
Simple, straightforward core gameplay: move, teleport, aim with cursor, dodge yellow bullets, block red ones
Roguelike items create chaos that looks different every run
Bosses have interesting mechanics and require attention and care
Different planets play drastically differently (moving planet, spaceship orbiting), giving the best replayability
criticism: Runs feel repetitive: same biomes and same few bosses every time
Regular enemies are one-shot so only bosses pose a threat
Being overpowered almost every run makes it feel less rewarding and less unique
Meta progression is weak: a shop with random unknown items (others vanish when you pick one) and minimal, situational upgrades
Wants more bosses and more in-run content; unsure he will return to it
unique_points: The game shows an error message when too many bullets fill the screen and need to be removed
Unlockable planets change the playstyle radically, such as a moving planet or a spaceship not on the planet
Simple extra block mechanic for red bullets used sparingly
commentary.quote: it is a fun mess for sure
design_criteria: Visuals/charm: hand-drawn paper style is cute though not for everybody
Power fantasy balance: being overpowered is satisfying but hurts reward when constant
Core gameplay: simple and enjoyable controls and mechanics
Item variety: cool items that create different chaos each run
Boss design: mechanic-driven bosses demanding attention
Run variety/content: same biomes and few bosses make runs repetitive
Meta progression: weak, opaque random unlock shop and minimal upgrades
Replayability: driven mainly by distinct playable planets

community.one_liner: A planet-defender arcade roguelike from Doodlegames (published by 2 Left Thumbs) where you fend off waves and bosses from a stationary circular planet with a hand-drawn, Flash-style look, using wildly synergistic items, in 1-4 player local co-op.
community.consensus_summary: Paper Planet is a small, niche Steam roguelite rated Very Positive (about 84% of roughly 530 reviews, per Steam data pulled locally; the store page shows 89% of 380 for one filter). Players like the doodle art, the chaotic item synergies and the couch co-op, and several say it is fun on sale. Complaints are about luck-dependent balance where you need a broken build or boss fights drag, a short content loop (one reviewer says they finished everything in about 2 hours), and achievements that have stayed broken for years. Critic coverage is essentially nonexistent: Metacritic has a page with no critic reviews and only one user rating, and no OpenCritic entry was found. Community threads include a 'Game abandoned?' topic, and a player review from 2026 says some achievements have been broken for over 2 years, so it reads as lightly supported since launch (Aug 2023). I could not retrieve patch notes, so update cadence is unconfirmed.
best_things: Hand-drawn, notebook-doodle, Flash-game art style that is coherent and charming
Item synergies are wacky and build-defining (bee-bullet swarms, electric walls, teleporting rocket bombs, bullet recycling)
1-4 player local couch co-op with Remote Play Together, good for chaotic party play
Lots of unlockable planets/characters, modes, modifiers and visuals tied to achievements
Option to skip the metaprogression grind and unlock everything immediately (praised by a 21-hour reviewer)
Fast, pick-up-and-play arcade runs with enough variety to be 'highly addictive' for a few hours
worst_things: Balance is lopsided: runs depend on getting a broken build, and without one boss fights become minutes of low-damage waiting
Most stats feel nearly meaningless; bullet count, fire rate and bullet recycling dominate while raw damage does little
At least 8 achievements reported broken for over 2 years, and '100% is bugged' is repeated in multiple reviews
Heavily luck-based, leaving little room for player skill according to some reviewers
Item upgrades lack descriptions, so players can't tell what they are picking (one review and a Steam discussion about item descriptions not showing)
Content runs out fast for some, with the loop feeling repetitive after an hour or two
Performance issues such as FPS drops in boss fights and lag from heavy bullet counts
Seen as too pricey for its content at $14.99 by at least one reviewer, even on discount
improvements: Fix the long-broken achievements so 100% completion is possible
Rebalance damage vs. fire rate/bullet count so that stats matter and weak runs are not a slog
Show clear item and upgrade descriptions in-game
Fix boss-fight FPS drops and raise the damage-counter integer cap (requested in Steam threads)
Add more content and variety to extend replay beyond a few hours
Visible developer communication and updates, since players ask whether the game is abandoned
unique_things: You defend a fixed circular planet that cannot move, described by one reviewer as Asteroids without movement
Blend of arcade bullet-hell shooter and tower-defense style planet defense
Flash/doodle aesthetic with a school-notebook vibe, cartoony and family friendly
Items combine freely with each other, leading to absurd overpowered runs
Local co-op for up to four players on one screen
A switch to unlock all metaprogression immediately, unusual for the genre
tedious_or_disliked: Boss fights that take minutes when your build is weak and you deal little damage
Waves of high-health enemies that become boring without good items
Repetitive feeling after the first hour or two for some players
Chaotic screen with no item descriptions, making it hard to read what is happening
divisive_points: Randomness: some love wild, chaotic build luck; others find it too luck-driven with too little skill
Value: some call it a great casual game, others say it is too expensive and too short for the price
Chaos level: fun mayhem for some, unreadable for others who bounced in under an hour
community.reception_notes: Released Aug 21, 2023 on Windows only (no Mac/Linux), $14.99. Launch reception was positive among Steam players and it has stayed Very Positive, but it never drew critic coverage (Metacritic lists 0 critic reviews and a single 7/10 user rating from March 2024, with both scores 'tbd'). Steam discussions show user concern about abandonment, unlockable achievements that never worked, and FPS drops during bosses; a 2026 review says achievements have been broken for over 2 years, suggesting sparse post-launch support. I could not fetch patch notes or Reddit (Reddit blocked, WebSearch budget exhausted), so the update history is unverified. Revenue and owner figures are third-party estimates, not audited numbers.
